children: Bank of America (BAC) Q3: net income $6.9B, GAAP EPS $0.91 (adj $1.08), revenue ~$30B, net interest income ~$16.4B, NII yield ~2.16%. $1.2B regulatory charge; shares slid ~5–9% intraday.
OCC found long‑running AML failures at Bank of America (BAC): under‑resourced compliance, weak transaction monitoring and poor customer due diligence. OCC issued a settlement and continues oversight.
Bank of America (BAC) held $109B in unrealized losses on its investment securities in September, up from $85B in June, mainly in MBS, U.S. Treasuries and agency bonds; most are held-to-maturity.
Bank of America (BAC) must hire an independent reviewer to examine past transactions, flag previously missed suspicious activity, and report findings to FinCEN as part of remediation.
Bank of America (BAC) said a regulatory consent order does not cap assets or restrict other business activities, addressing trader concerns about limits on operations or the balance sheet.
Bank of America moved about 1,000 employees into anti-money-laundering and compliance roles via internal transfers, reshaping staff to bolster AML and compliance operations per regulatory needs.
Bank of America hired about 1,000 contractors to fix software vulnerabilities flagged by Anthropic's AI tool Mythos, focusing on patching flaws; reports cite the headcount and remediation work.
OCC report says Bank of America (BAC) and other big banks sometimes denied clients banking services for political, religious or other reasons; the report imposed no fines or penalties on BAC.
Analysts covering Bank of America Corp (BAC) rate it as Buy: all 25 tracked analysts list holds or buys, median 12‑month price target $66, about 18% above last close $53.96.
